label: copy-phase input j (fed-back j at original position >= 2)
explanation: Token detector for the letter j as a copy-phase input, i.e. when the model has just re-emitted a j and that j is fed back. All activation mass is in the copy phase and essentially all of it is on in_tok == j; it never fires on j in the original phase or at the delimiter. It is weak or silent when the fed-back j is one of the first two original tokens (recall_idx <= 2; e.g. at recall_idx 2 it fires weakly, around 0.1-0.3 of max), and from recall_idx >= 3 on it fires about 3.3% of copy steps. The strongest activations are when the j is near the end of the sequence (to_go 0-1, e.g. a f j k <DEL> a f [j]). The remaining false positives are mostly j at original position 2 in long sequences (L = 7-9), where it sometimes stays silent. Output token, previous tokens, and first token have essentially no effect.

issues: Minor: the explanation says activations at recall_idx<=2 reach only about 0.1-0.3 of max. On the test split the missed activations include 0.58 ('1 j d <DEL> 1 [j]', L=3) and 0.41 ('r j j <DEL> r [j]'). Short sequences (L=3-4) can fire moderately at recall_idx=2. These misses hold only 2.7% of activation mass.

The false positives are systematic but the explanation already discloses them: j at recall_idx==3 with L>=7 is active only 49% of the time (8300 predicted steps, 1.1% of mass). By contrast, recall_idx==3 with L<=6 has precision 0.99 and recall_idx>=4 has precision 1.00. The feature looks like a graded function of position and outputs remaining, not a hard cutoff at recall_idx 3. No alternative predicate improved test F1 by more than 0.002 (best was to_go<=4 & (recall_idx>=3 | L==3): F1 0.937).

Verified claims: 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase. in_tok j carries all the mass (fewer than 50 active steps on any other token). Nothing fires in the original or delimiter phases. to_go 0-1 carries 67% of the mass, and the top examples are j at to_go 0. out_tok, prev_tok and first_tok show flat lift. The reported test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.926, R 0.945, F1 0.936, mass recall 0.973).
